question: Should the RFC’s cross-product localization architecture proceed as a staged core program, or should localization remain limited to owner-specific surfaces until a narrower contract is approved?
rationale: The PR introduces a new shared package and presentation contract across protocol, core, UI, channels, skills, and plugins; choosing the permanent boundary and rollout order is a maintainer product and ownership decision, not a mechanical repair.

options.title: Sponsor a staged localization program
options.body: Approve the RFC direction, land prerequisite slices first, and require each rebased slice to have an owner-scoped review and upgrade proof.

options.title: Narrow to existing owner surfaces
options.body: Retain only independently justified CLI, UI, or channel-local improvements and defer the shared package and protocol expansion.

options.title: Pause the series
options.body: Keep the RFC open but defer implementation until maintainers allocate ownership for the shared localization and plugin-contract surfaces.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a staged localization program
recommendation.body: Approve the RFC direction, land prerequisite slices first, and require each rebased slice to have an owner-scoped review and upgrade proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The contributor authored the RFC-linked foundation series and can provide the intended boundary and staged split, while final acceptance remains a maintainer decision.
